questions.answer: Fairly, yes. I like to keep things in order, both my space and my schedule, because clutter genuinely stresses me out. A little organisation up front spares me a lot of [[hassle]] later.

questions.q: How do you keep track of your tasks?
questions.answer: I rely mostly on my phone's calendar and a simple to-do list. At work I'm handling applications for lots of students with different deadlines, so writing everything down is [[non-negotiable]] for me.

questions.q: Are you more productive in the morning or the evening?
questions.answer: Definitely the morning. My mind is [[sharpest]] then, so I tackle my hardest tasks early. By the evening my focus fades, so I save lighter activities for later in the day.

questions.q: Were you organised when you were a child?
questions.answer: Not at all, I'm afraid. My school bag was always a mess and I was forever losing pencils. My mother [[despaired of]] me at times, so being organised is definitely something I learned later in life.

questions.q: Do you think it's important for students to be organised?
questions.answer: Absolutely, and I see it every day in my job. The students who stay organised tend to meet deadlines calmly, while the others end up [[scrambling]] at the last minute and making careless mistakes on their applications.
